key_insight: The twist angle in WS2-graphene heterostructures significantly affects ultrafast charge separation efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Understanding twist angle effects is crucial for optimizing van der Waals heterostructures in photovoltaics and optoelectronics.
method: Utilized time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (trARPES).
Probed ultrafast charge transfer in epitaxially grown heterostructures.
Tested twist angles of 0° and 30° under photoexcitation at ħω = 3.1 eV.
evidence_signal: Efficient charge separation was observed at 0° twist angle, contrasting with similar electron and hole transfer rates at 30°.
watch_item: Further investigations are needed to understand the full implications of twist angle on charge dynamics in various heterostructures.
paper_title: Influence of twist angle on ultrafast charge separation in WS2-graphene heterostructures
